title: Historical medical/attendance evidence separation and filing pattern
summary: The correspondence archive contains a dedicated employee medical-document folder separate from disciplinary files. It holds an image-only attendance calendar plus date-named smartphone screenshot images. Together with the 2013 FMLA routing instruction, this supports a historical record-separation pattern for medical/leave evidence.

claims.claim: The archive stores employee medical material under a dedicated Employee Medical Docs hierarchy separate from disciplinary-warning files.

evidence.note: Employee identity and medical content remain restricted.

claims.claim: The supplied medical folder contains one two-page image-only attendance-calendar PDF and 18 PNG images, with the PNGs uniformly 1080x2460 pixels and filenames organized by relevant dates.

evidence.note: Only file type/count/dimensions/date-label structure were analyzed; medical image content was not promoted.

claims.claim: The repeated date-named screenshots alongside an attendance calendar suggest a historical workflow of linking supporting medical/attendance evidence to specific absence dates while keeping that evidence in a restricted medical location.

evidence.note: Interpretation is based on organization/naming only, not medical content.

trigger: HR receives medical/FMLA/attendance supporting evidence related to an employee absence.
prerequisites: The related attendance/leave event can be linked without copying medical content into general records.
steps: Store medical/leave supporting evidence in a restricted medical location rather than the general disciplinary/timekeeping record.
Associate evidence with the relevant attendance/leave date using restricted metadata.
Maintain an attendance-facing record that can reference protected/approved status without exposing medical details.
Preserve source-date provenance for each supporting artifact.
decisions: Whether a document contains medical/FMLA information requiring restricted handling.
How to link supporting evidence to attendance without duplicating protected content.
controls: Medical evidence must not be embedded in general personnel, disciplinary, or timesheet packets solely for convenience.
Generalized knowledge may retain only workflow/metadata patterns, never diagnoses, treatment details or employee-specific medical facts.
Image-only documents should be classified using visible/structural cues and date metadata, with OCR output remaining restricted if performed.
unresolved_questions: What is the current official storage location and retention schedule for employee medical/FMLA documentation?
Is the historical attendance calendar still used, and if so how is it reconciled with ADP or other attendance systems?
What restricted metadata should link medical documentation to an attendance event without exposing the document itself?
automation_candidates: Medical-document classifier that automatically routes image/PDF evidence into a restricted medical queue.
Attendance linkage model that stores document hash/date/status references rather than copying medical content.
Duplicate/near-duplicate detection for repeated screenshots or overlapping date evidence.

provenance.notes: Only folder structure, file types, dimensions, counts and date-oriented naming were generalized.
